title: Grow tool: grow a part from a click up to its grooves, and turn its outline into rings (Ctrl+U)
user-messages:
> The grow tool and the connection tool’s additions

split into two tickets
description:
A ring-scene tool (Ctrl+U) that grows a part from a click outward until it reaches the grooves round it, and turns the grown patch's outline into rings. Split out of the stroke-segmentation worktree (CRAW-105), where it was built without a ticket.

## What exists

`GrowTool` (the tool), `GrownPatch` (the region growing), the Ctrl+U tool switch in `RingScene`, a line in the connection package's `package-info.java` and one in `ARCHITECTURE.md`.

## What the review found

From ai-workspace `reports/craw-105-uncommitted-review-2026-11-12.md` (parts 4 and 5):

- Hand-picked numbers with no ticket listing them: pocket ratios 20 and 4 in `GrownPatch`; 0.05, 6 and 16 in `GrowTool`.
- No tests.
- `GrownPatch.faceCount` is flagged as a debugging counter and is read by the tool's status line.
- New log lines in `GrowTool`.
- The tool overrides and clears the same `regions` look id that `RegionLayer` uses, which can clear the region colours until `RegionLayer`'s own state next changes.
definition-of-done: 1. Every number the growing and the tool use is listed on this ticket for the user to decide. 2. Unit tests cover the region growing on a shape with known grooves. 3. The tool no longer clears the region colours. 4. A launch.json entry and a screenshot under tmp/ show a part grown on a scan.
testing-plan: 1. Unit test: on a torus with two grooves across its tube, growing from a click between them stops at both grooves. 2. Unit test: the grown patch's outline becomes closed rings lying in those grooves. 3. Run the tool on a crawfish scan and screenshot a grown part.
unknowns: Does BisectorTool.draftAlong (a bisector along a drawn or grown line) belong here, with the connection tool ticket, or with stroke segmentation?
